summary:
Slice 4's engine treats a transform as data: a TransformDraft (the window's cards, each field with a state: frozen, open, fuzzy or keep-empty). One pure analysis, analyseTransform, covers TR-11 (with G6), TR-12 (a), TR-13 and TR-15, and it computes only what visible items allow (RV-6 b4). One pure planner, planTypedWrite, writes what you typed and telelean's follow-on edits.

Outside a session the plan becomes one board action, apply-transform: TR-15's direct path, one Undo step, using TR-12's checks only. It freezes the fields you typed as standing freezes, extending D3-44, and drops worded_by: agent from a typed sentence (G5).

Everything else runs as a new queue step kind, 'transform'. telelean writes the typed content, checks it, then gives Claude a turn when the transform needs one. Claude's part reuses slice 3's whole-model tools under a narrow transform scope: propose_arrow, remove_arrow, mark_proof_broken, add_card and request_unfreeze, with G5's field allowances. The step writes no proofs and changes no kinds (S8, CF-4). It is all or nothing: a step that does not pass is taken back whole, and its transform stays queued.

What you typed becomes one 'typed:<card>' item per card. telelean records each unit it wrote in a new ledger entry (`typed`, outside ws/), and only those units count as yours. The item is accepted as yours (RV-7 b5) once its RV-5 dependencies are accepted. Content copied from Claude stays in Claude's item, which returns to review marked "updated" (TR-15, DO-2).

Freezes:
- The transform reason (FZ-7 r4) gets real values.
- A revalue map makes your own change the frozen value (FZ-3 2e).
- Sessions started by Transform cards… get binding session-start freezes (D3-1's hook made real).

Two narrowings:
- No run exists while you draft outside a session. The session starts at Submit transform, and a stale draft is refused.
- A Submit review that carries out transforms seals the session stack and opens a new stage.

TR-12 (b) elaborates your typed Lean against your own files at the model root, so nothing hidden can leak. Typed Lean that names things not yet in your files is written verbatim by Claude, which a new gate rule, `typed-text`, enforces.

The plan has 21 logged D4 decisions and 10 sub-slices (4a1, 4a2, 4b1, 4b2, 4b3, 4c in core, strictly in sequence; then 4d, 4f, 4e, 4g in the runner and host), plus a conditional 4x for D3-43's fallback.

open_questions: Typed content representation (D4-1). Recommended: one typed:<card> item per card, owned unit by unit from the ledger, accepted as yours once its dependencies are accepted. Claude's copied content stays in Claude's items. Alternative: a moving baseline Y = B + typed, with items computed against Y. Its Rejects are cleaner, but typed Lean that uses Claude's vocabulary would make Y fail to build, and every slice-2/3 call site would need Y instead of B.

Drafting outside a session (D4-2). Recommended: no run until Submit transform; the draft lives in the host's storage and is refused when stale. Alternative: ES-3's literal provisional session (a run from window opening that locks the board and holds B and the session-start freezes), which costs a shadow per opened window.

Submit with transforms (D4-4). Recommended: always seal and open a new stage, even when only no-Claude transforms were queued. Alternative: go straight to the end confirmation as RV-12 says, which needs Back to review to invert the typed write and its records.

Rollback granularity (D4-3). Recommended: all or nothing per transform; a step that does not pass takes its typed write back too, and the transform stays queued. Alternative: keep the typed write when its own check passed and only Claude's part failed (one more rollback rule).

TR-12 (b) basis (D4-5). Recommended: elaborate against your files at the model root (the board's own build, which is B while a session locks the board). Names not in your files, Claude's proposals included, are written verbatim by Claude under the typed-text rule. Alternative: elaborate against the working copy. That accepts Claude's visible vocabulary at once, but needs hiding of proof-phase names (RV-6) and switching the session mirror between B and the head.

Claude's values copied into a window (D4-7). Recommended: they start open and marked, because TR-4's frozen copies exist to protect your own Lean (S11). Alternative: TR-4 literally, so a Decline → Transform of a Formalize item keeps Claude's Lean unless you unfreeze it.

D2-15 (D4-9). Recommended: keep it for Formalize-origin Shaky rework; transform-origin rework follows that transform's TR-7 setting, and splits of your cards go through Decline → Transform. Alternative: lift it by giving Submit steps add_card, with TR-7 (c)'s always-allowed splits.

Make it pending, TR-14 (d) (D4-8). Recommended: after Apply, through the board's existing Mark pending on the now unproved card. Alternative: an Accept option on Proof broken that writes the pending claim in the session as a due write, like the premise write, with its recovery cases.

Suggested premises, TR-10 (a) and the user's TRANSFORM 9 (D4-11). Recommended: a window on an Add premise edits only its draft's sentence, Why and Lean statement; it is re-checked and then accepted with holdAs. Alternative: not offered (narrows the user's explicit words); or convert it into a new card of yours plus an arrow.

Session targets in a transform (D4-16). Recommended: the proof is locked, trashing is refused, and the statement may change only when your files have no proof of it, with the Result reworked in the same queue. Alternative: let a target's Result become a Proof broken item, which D3-47 forbids today.

Direct application's freezes (D4-13). Recommended: freeze the fields you typed on existing cards as standing freezes in the same Undo step (FROZEN 1, TR-5, D3-44). Alternative: freeze nothing, reading ES-3's 'its freezes are undone' literally.

Session-start freezes (D4-14). Recommended: whole cards, vocabulary included, for every card not in the window, lifted per key by Unfreeze for the session. Alternative: only axiom and proposition cards, leaving vocabulary open to the transform step's whole-subject view.

In-session kind changes needing D-11's rewrite (D4-10). Recommended: refuse them in a session. Alternative: carry out the rewrite as typed units on the dependents' proofs, which needs proof-text ownership by typed items.

New cards with a fuzzy sentence (D4-12). Recommended: slots that Claude fills with add_card, with no typed arrow to a slot. Alternative: require you to type every new card's sentence (narrows TR-4 and the user's TRANSFORM 4).

Building slice 4 before slice 3's 3c1 tools exist. Recommended: no; 4b2 and 4f reuse remove_arrow, mark_proof_broken and G5 allowances, so slice 4 starts after slice 3 is verified. Alternative: duplicate minimal tool validators in slice 4 (parallel machinery, against the simplicity directive).
safety_notes: S8 (transform steps write no proofs, TR-14 a). Enforced by the 'transform' code's no-proofs token and B.4 (no .holds kind change except typed units). Step limits fix every theorem except mark_proof_broken's removals. freeze_statements and propose_assumption are refused in transform steps. Tested by judge cheats (theorem, replaced proof, completed pending) and the FakeBackend transform-cheat-proof script, which gives up after three attempts.

S10 (typed Lean can do more than you see). Enforced by typedLeanProblems: the single-term rule, G0's forbidden-text scan including init and hygienic names, one declaration per vocabulary field, the shape rule, and no theorem. It runs in the window, at Submit, and again in planTypedWrite and planTransformDirect (fail closed). Tested by cheat cases in typedLean.test.ts plus the planner's refusal tests.

S11 (copied Lean starts frozen). makeTransformDraft starts your copied Lean, Dependencies and Proof frozen, and the transform reason persists for the session, so a later mid-stage Formalize cannot weaken it. Claude's proposed copies start open but remain Claude's items, which need Accept (RV-7 c1). Tested by a judge test of weakening a frozen copy, and by a session test with a mid-stage Formalize after a transform.

S9's other half and TR-13 (inside a session nothing is left broken; G4). In a session the choices are only Claude (unfrozen) or delete, and a frozen dependent is a problem. The S0 check refuses errors outside the declared dependents. No .holds is left behind by a trash. Outside a session, Delete anyway needs an explicit confirmation. Tested in analyse.test.ts, plan.test.ts and the FakeBackend give-up script.

You never lose the right to decide what counts (RV-7 b5, §14.5). A typed item is yours only for units telelean wrote: ledger entries live outside ws/, so Claude cannot write them, and ownership requires the judged value to equal the recorded one. Auto-accept happens only at a queue end that wrote those units, and only when its RV-5 dependencies are accepted. The backstop re-derives typed ownership from B, F and the ledger. Tested by a forged-value test (unowned), the auto-accept fixpoint tests, and backstop refusals.

Copied Claude content is never accepted by submitting a window (TR-15, DO-2). The no-Claude-content rule records no typed unit where Claude content remains; that change stays in Claude's item, which returns to review 'updated'. Tested by a reconcile test (updated, not accepted) and a FakeBackend DO-2 session.

Only you change kinds (CF-4, §14.10). G5 refuses any `type:` change but a typed unit's, B.4's theorem-to-axiom exception is typed-only, and Claude has no kind tool. Tested by a judge cheat that changes `type:` in a transform step, and by a typed P→A passing with its unit.

Frozen binds Claude only, and your own change becomes the frozen value (FZ-1, FZ-3 2e). revalued is written only by typed writes, from the judgement of the typed state, and only for the units' own targets and held names. Accepted items whose content you change leave accepted through the confirmed cascade (RV-5 b3) instead of being revalued. Tested by freeze table tests, and by a session test where your typed change to a standing-frozen field leaves no stage problem while Claude's later change of it is refused.

Transform-started sessions freeze everything not selected (INITIATING 2, FZ-7 r2, D3-1 made real). effectiveFreezes derives session-start entries expected at B. Unfreeze lifts them per key only by your action, and FZ-8 restores them at the end. Tested by a judge test changing a non-window card (refused) and the end rows.

Meaning before proof (RV-6). The window copies come from the masked view; analysis and cascades run on the masked state while results are hidden; TR-12's scratch uses your files, never the working copy; session targets' proofs are locked. Transform-step items are all listed items, never Results' parts. Tested by twin non-interference tests (byte-identical drafts, analyses and SessionView with a hidden Result proved or not).

The base never moves, and stale work is refused (ES-7). A draft carries its basis, and the host refuses it when the files changed. TR-12 refuses on drift or stale facts. A queued transform is recomputed at Submit and refused when anything relevant changed. Tested by host tests with a hand edit between opening and Submit.

Undo never crosses Claude, and the two stacks never mix (UN-1, UN-5). Queue, drop and replace are session-stack steps checked by the reducer. Submit with transforms seals. The direct path is a board step only outside sessions. Tested by reducer stack property tests and an Undo stopping at Submit's seal.

Atomicity and reload (ES-6). The typed write is inside its step: the ledger entry is written before files, the step's rollback covers a crash, and all-or-nothing keeps the transform queued. Drafts persist in the host store or run.json. Tested by reload tests mid-step (interrupted, then Resume or Cancel step) and with an open draft.

Resources (the user's RAM rule). One TR-12 Lean job per Submit transform, under runExclusive and the memory guard, at the model root and read-only. Transform steps use slice 2's per-step caps.
